title: Permutations II
prompt:
Given a collection of numbers `nums` that might contain duplicates, return all possible unique permutations, in any order.

For deterministic comparison, sort the outer list of permutations (for example, by converting each permutation to a tuple and sorting the list of tuples).

examples.explanation: Only 3 distinct orderings exist since the two 1's are indistinguishable.
When every element is identical, all n! orderings collapse into a single unique permutation.

hints: This is Permutations but nums may contain duplicates — the standard 'try every unused index' backtracking will now produce the same permutation multiple times.
Sort nums first so equal values are adjacent, then track which indices are used just like standard permutations.

At each recursive call, skip index i if nums[i] == nums[i-1] and index i-1 hasn't been used yet in the current path — this forces equal values to be placed in a fixed relative order across branches, eliminating duplicate permutations without ever comparing full paths.

solution.approach: Sort nums so duplicate values sit next to each other, then backtrack over which index to place next using a 'used' boolean array. The duplicate-avoidance rule: skip candidate index i if nums[i] equals nums[i-1] and nums[i-1] is currently NOT used. This ensures that among a run of equal values, they are only ever placed in left-to-right index order within any given path, so two different index choices can never produce the identical output permutation. Everything else mirrors standard permutation backtracking: mark used, append to path, recurse, then undo.
solution.code:
def permute_unique(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    n = len(nums)
    result = []
    path = []
    used = [False] * n

    def backtrack():
        if len(path) == n:
            result.append(path[:])
            return
        for i in range(n):
            if used[i]:
                continue
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1] and not used[i - 1]:
                continue
            used[i] = True
            path.append(nums[i])
            backtrack()
            path.pop()
            used[i] = False

    backtrack()
    result.sort(key=lambda perm: tuple(perm))
    return result
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n * n!) for the output, O(n) recursion depth
